The buhay is a friction drum, Hornbostel–Sachs 232.11-92. Its body is a conical barrel, sometimes made from a wooden tub, covered at one end with a goatskin pierced in the middle, through which passes a bundle of horsehair knotted at its end. Playing usually takes two people: one holds the instrument and the other draws wet fingers over the hair; recent versions are held by the foot and can be played by one person. The instrument is found in Ukraine, with local variants in Romania, Moldova, Hungary, Lithuania, Poland and elsewhere.
